Source: A 2-year-old boy is brought to the emergency room by his mother, who states that her son has been coughing uncontrollably for 3 hours.
The child has a medical history of obesity and atopic dermatitis and uses topical steroid cream.
His temperature is 98.5°F (36.9°C), pulse is 120/min, blood pressure is 90/52 mmHg, and respirations are 32/min.
A chest radiograph is performed and the results are shown in Figures A and B.
On exam, he appears uncomfortable, is coughing continuously, and is drooling.
His family history is notable for asthma in his older sister and irritable bowel syndrome in his father.
Cardiopulmonary and abdominal exams are unremarkable.
